inlineContent.text: BlueGPS locates the device with its own antennas by default. Installed in the building,
they pick up the Bluetooth tag the device broadcasts, in the background too, and the
BlueGPS server computes the position. BlueGPS also works with other positioning systems
compatible with it, which compute the position on the device: from the building’s
magnetic field and the device’s sensors, or from the beacons installed in the building.
A position reaches the SDK in one of two ways:
From the BlueGPS antennas.
The SDK broadcasts the device’s tag over Bluetooth, the
antennas pick it up, and the BlueGPS server computes the position, which
reads.
From a supported positioning system on the device.

positioning.alt: Two ways a position reaches the SDK. By default, the BlueGPS antennas: the SDK broadcasts a tag, the antennas pick it up, and the BlueGPS server computes the position, which the map shows. Or a supported positioning system on the device, from the magnetic field and the device’s sensors or from beacons in the building: your app hands each fix to BGPSPositionCoordinator, which posts it to the map.
